utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, good morning, everybody. I'm sorry for the delay. I guess that's because of changing of the courtroom. And later on we have to get used to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I have been informed that the witness lost his way in this building, so Mr. Usher is trying to locate him. Well, during this period, I would like to know whether there's anything procedural that both parties would like to bring to the attention of this Trial Chamber. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I can inform the Chamber that for some time now we have listed generically on our witness list a witness from the British battalion to authenticate some British battalion documents that had come up in the trial before. And based on contacts with the British Ministry of Defence, I am prepared to say at this time that the witness that will be provided for that purpose is named Alistair Rule, R-U-L-E. We expect Mr. Rule to testify on Thursday. I wouldn't expect it to be terribly long testimony. I can advise at this time I believe he testified as a Prosecution witness in the Kordic case but on matters -- well, I say obviously -- presumably substantially different than this case since that case related to central Bosnia. As soon as we have any additional information to provide to counsel or the Court, we will do so, but that is the name of the individual whose -- the name I've received to be that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since we still did not find the witness, we'll break for ten minutes. --- Break taken at 9.15 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we are extremely sorry about the delay, since we announced the changing of the courtroom and the time yesterday. I guess nobody could trust, so-called automatic pilot in this building. But anyway, we have to make up the time we have lost in some later stage, because we have to be fair to the parties for the time allocated to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes. Examined by Mr. Poriouvaev: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AC, yesterday we came to the point that one operation was carried out in Mostar, and apart from your unit, Stela's unit and the 4th Battalion were involved in that operation. Now, I would like you to direct to an Exhibit P774. It was already on your desk yesterday. But before we proceed with this document, I've got one more question to ask. And this question will be: You explained to the Trial Chamber that you fulfilled several kinds of jobs on the confrontation line, and one of the functions was just to guard the confrontation line. Could you expand a little bit more. What do they mean by ordering you to guard the confrontation line? From whom?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order for the -- for the guards during the conflict came from Baja, from Mario Milicevic, Baja, and that was one of the easiest jobs, that is, to stand guard and keep alert throughout the duty. That was the task of the guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was not allowed to appear in the area of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians were not allowed to be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you allowed to shoot at people who appear on the confrontation line without permission?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One was authorised to fire at anything moving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without warning?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without any warning, because the defence line itself was a warning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your unit have sniper positions on the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember in which buildings were they deployed?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which buildings?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These buildings are practically on the defence front line but a little bit withdrawn, so that there wasn't much danger and yet I had a good view of the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever perform your functions as a sniper?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's proceed with a document -- with Exhibit 774. And you have it in both English and B/C/S versions. Which one would you prefer? I think that you have a B/C/S version only. But it doesn't matter. I would like you to take a look at the letterhead of the document. First off, the front page. What is this document about? Is it possible to read?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can make out some of it, but not all. I can read the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. At least, what you understood. What did you understand from the document? What's the subject matter?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should be the report of ill-treated and killed persons, prisoners, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's turn to the first page. Take a look at the left upper corner. Do you see any letterhead there?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you see there?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see a stamp of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna, Ministry of Defence, military police administration, military post code 1711.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see a seal to the right of the stamp?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I would like the witness to go to number 45 in the document. I would like you to take a look at the last column of the document. Do you see any names that are familiar to you there? 45, and the last column, to the right. The last to the right.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can recognise when it says here, "80 group, Benko Penavic."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see another name in this same column?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 45. Are you reading number 45?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me look at 45 once again. Oh, yes. Yes, I do see. I see the name Mario Zubac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday in your testimony, you claimed that it was not only yourself but some other soldiers who were authorised to take -- to pick up prisoners from Heliodrom. Among them you mentioned Zubac. Do you see here the same Zubac?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I direct you now to the second column from the left side, 45. Do you see the list of three persons who are alleged to have been killed?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. Do you see the list of some persons under number 45 which are claimed to be killed -- who are claimed to be killed?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but none of them sounds familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see the list of four wounded persons?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those names familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see the date in column 3, under the same number, 45?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Read the date.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 27th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go down to number 46. Do you see the list of 29 persons, prisoners who are alleged to have been killed? I would ask you to look through the list and tell me if you can recall any of the names familiar to you. If you don't remember, don't remember. Do you see any names that are familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see the date when the persons -- prisoners were taken from Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is the date?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 27th September 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit was in charge of them, according to the last column?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's turn to number 54. Do you see the list of seven people, prisoners, who are alleged to have been killed? Do you see any names that are familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the date when the prisoners were taken from Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Excuse me. Yes, it says the 22nd September 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now we will go to column 5. That's about the unit and the person who was in charge of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Could you repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which column?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last column. That's about the unit that was in charge of prisoners and the person who took them.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says the ATG Benko Penavic; and the person responsible, Mario Zubac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now let's go to number 57. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see among the list of people who are alleged as having been wounded any names that are familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And take a look at the date.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is September 18th, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the unit, according to the last column?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's ATG Benko Penavic; and the person responsible for prisoners, Andrija Novak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now that I see it written down. Perhaps it wouldn't have come to me otherwise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now turn to number 74. Do you see any name of person who is alleged to have been wounded?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The date?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: September 1st, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The unit in charge?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ATG group Benko Penavic; and the person responsible, Miroslav Zadro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember Miroslav Zadro?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, let's go to number 80. Do you see the name of Mirsad Kurtovic who is alleged to have been wounded?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did it happen, according to this document?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened on the 31st of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit was in charge of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: ATG Benko Penavic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar -- were you familiar with Mirsad Kurtovic?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. You may put aside this document. Somewhere in the beginning of your testimony you have claimed that you knew a person whose nickname was Tuta. Did you ever personally see him?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it happen during the war, before the war, or after the war?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was during the war. I saw him when we were on our way to Prozor for the first time, at the headquarters of Siroki Brijeg, the old tobacco station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that that location, Duhanska Stanica was the headquarters of Stela's unit -- I'm sorry, Tuta's unit. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a soldier, so I suppose I was expected to know where the headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you just recount here in the courtroom the situation in which you saw Mr. Tuta. What happened on that day in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, at this point I would object to this line of questioning. We've had somewhat of a minor preview, and that is Prozor, Prozor. This situation, Your Honour -- and I know that the Trial Chamber has not been allowed and not had the opportunity to review the witness statement, but the Defence has, and we lodge a strenuous objection to any testimony concerning Prozor. It's outside the scope of the indictment. It has no relevance, therefore, to this case, and this is a situation where we strongly and firmly believe that the allowance of this type of evidence into this Trial Chamber and into this trial is for the sole purpose of insinuating that if a person such as an accused were to do something on a prior occasion, therefore he did something on a latter occasion or subsequent occasion. But the evidence which they wish to elicit through this witness at this time goes to Prozor. It's not alleged in the indictment. It's not an issue in this case, and we believe that it's highly prejudicial. The probative value is outweighed by the prejudicial value to the accused in his right to a fair trial should you let this evidence come in. And I object on those grounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we don't have the summary of this witness at our hands. We would like to hear the response from the Prosecutor about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will do it with pleasure. I suggest that my learned colleague is too fast. First of all, for that moment, we are still in Siroki Brijeg. I have not asked him -- I mean, the witness any question about Prozor yet. Anyway, anyway, if you look at paragraph -- from 14 through 17 of the indictment, that's about Mr. Naletilic's superior authority, and you -- if you look in the Background part of your indictment where the areas are enumerated, are indicated, Prozor is also indicated. I'm not that interested in the operation carried out in Prozor, at least at this point, and I will not ask any questions about the operations itself. But anything which is relevant to Mr. Naletilic's higher position should be considered as relevant to our case, and not going beyond the scope of our examination-in-chief beyond the indictment itself. That is the Prosecution's position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek. Do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. President, I believe that my learned colleague is slightly and absolutely mistaken. Under paragraphs 14 through 17, Superior Authority would only go to the superior authority of my client within the context of the framework of the indictment, not in some other area of Bosnia or Herzegovina or Kosovo, or any other location, but only within the framework of the indictment. And as far as background goes, Your Honour, this is not, I submit -- we submit, the Defence, that this is not background information due to the time frame of the situation. So on both occasions, either Superior Authority or Background, it's highly inadmissible, irrelevant, not contained within the context of the scope of this indictment, introduced merely for the purpose to prejudice our client; the probative value is outweighed strongly by the prejudicial effect this testimony will have on this Trial Chamber, and we strenuously and strongly object, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: May I respond, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you have to be very concise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Very concise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: First of all, Prozor area was mentioned in paragraph 8 of the indictment, the area where the conflict started in October 1992. And it was at that time ongoing conflict. And the events I would like to direct my witness, happened before he left his unit, and he left his unit in November 1993. So all my questions will go to the period within the scope of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we believe that the paragraph 8 of the indictment mentioned Prozor. That's true. But as for the time frame, it's out of the time frame of this indictment. And Mr. Prosecutor, you may continue your question concerning the event happened in Siroki Brijeg at this moment, while bearing in mind the objections from Defence counsel. You may proceed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: All right. All right. Now I would like Witness AC to be shown Exhibit 26.9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you identify this location?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please inform the Trial Chamber which location was identified by yourself.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the old tobacco station at Siroki Brijeg where Tuta's headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see Tuta inside of the building or outside of the building?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was outside of that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could indicate it on this -- in this picture, the precise place where you saw him.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take a pointer.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was approximately here, near this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take a marker and just encircle the area and put number "1" there.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You may take away the exhibit from the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the task set for your unit in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Mr. President, I object to the form of that question. It assumes facts not in evidence. The question says, What was your task? and there's been no evidence that this witness nor anybody with him on that date had been given any tasks. So I object to the form of the question. It assumes facts not in evidence and in fact becomes leading and suggestive also when taken in that context. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, you are too fast in this question. You may pose it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: All right. I'll just abide by your ruling, just not to go into details of Prozor operation. That's why I tried to limit myself to some certain questions relevant to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Witness AC, did you see any other commanders in Siroki Brijeg along with Mr. Naletilic on that day?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My commander was there, Milicevic, Baja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they have any meeting there?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tuta gave a small speech.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at this speech?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what was that speech about?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were talking about going in the field, in the same Prozor that we have mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your unit the only one that was presented at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. I think, if I remember well, Tuta's unit, which was in Siroki Brijeg, was also there. Perhaps not the full complement, but I think that they were also there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Since the Trial Chamber does not allow me to put any questions relevant to Prozor, I will skip this part of my prepared direct examination. Witness, we were talking about the confrontation line and the division of the confrontation line in Mostar, and now I would like to return to this subject, just to clarify some issues. Did you ever go to Stela's unit headquarters?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see his headquarters?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the building located?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was located near our base, about 200 metres -- two to three hundred metres in the direction of Balinovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it far away from your own headquarters?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the usher to show the witness Exhibit number P15.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell me if this photo rings a bell to you.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does ring a bell. It is -- it reminds me of Stela's headquarters, even though the building is more recent. But I can recognise it by the street and the wall that I would like to show.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate that street and the wall in the picture?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the pointer, and do that.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the wall. It was a characteristic wall. It extended along the whole length of the street. And I also am familiar with that street there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show, please. I don't see the street.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I would like you to put number "1" on the wall you have indicated and number "2" to the exit, to the street.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. You may take away this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AC, from your witness statement I learned that on some occasion you were wounded. When did it happen?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened on the 15th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a very serious wound?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And now I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit number P621.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Witness, I would like you to take a look at the original version of the document. But don't show it on the ELMO because otherwise the people will see your name. All right?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And I would like to just -- to call the attention of the Trial Chamber that in the draft translation of the document, in the left corner side, there is a slip -- a mistake -- a misprint, I would say. The unit called "Branko Penavic," but in the original document you have "Benko Penavic."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AC, who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My commander at the time, Mario Milicevic, Baja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the document signed in your presence?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have such kind of document before October 1993, when, according to the document, it was given to you?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Is it true that, according to this document, you were a member of the HVO from the 4th of April, 1992, and as from 9th of May, 1993, you were a member of the Benko Penavic unit?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And maybe -- perhaps, Witness, you will be able to explain to me one term that I have come across in this document. Your unit is called an elite unit. Did this document give you any powers, specific powers?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I will return to this question afterwards. But now perhaps you will explain, what did you understand by "elite unit"? Why were you called an "elite unit"?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were called the elite unit because we were a little bit different from everyone else. The difference consisted in that we had uniforms that were slightly different than the others. They were camouflage and green. They were quite different from all the other uniforms in various brigades and various battalions, and we were also involved in special tasks for which we were paid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the difference between your uniform and other units' uniforms?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was in the Benko Penavic uniform, the green uniforms that we had -- we were the only unit that we had. And the other camouflage uniforms that the other units had were different, both in colour and in quality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have anything on your uniform that indicated that you belonged to Benko Penavic unit?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any specific patches, badges, other signs of distinction?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have military ranks within the unit?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your commander, I mean your big commander, Milicevic, have any military rank?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had the rank of Major.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about your salary in comparison with other units? Was it at the same level?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not the same level of salary. ATG salaries were a little bit higher than the others had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have just mentioned that your unit was involved in some special operations. Perhaps you could explain to the Trial Chamber what your mean by "special operations."

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Special operations were the ethnic cleansing of Muslim civilians in the city of Mostar, then going to -- going in the field wherever there was danger of having the lines breached, and anything else that the HVO might need.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit number P556. You also have a B/C/S version. Witness, have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a problem. May we break? Because my learned colleagues from the bench or counsels just are making some signs to me. Since I am here just to -- to clarify when exactly we'll have our first break, official break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think that's a question we have to solve, because we are 30 minutes late. And how long are you going to take after the break for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, it will not take me more than 20 minutes. It's a maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. I'm afraid we have to break here. So Mr. Usher, would you please show the witness out of the room after pulling down the blinds. So we might have 65 or 70 minutes sitting after the break because we have to finish the morning session by 1.45. This courtroom will be used for another case this afternoon at 2.15. We were told that there have to be 30 minutes break between the two cases. So we will resume at 11.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. While we're waiting for the witness, I merely wanted to make an objection. That is, alongside the witness's statement, some documents were to be enclosed, that is, quite a number of documents, nine altogether, nine different types of documents, and the Defence considers these documents very important. I talked with my learned friend. I was promised those documents. However, since I evidently will not get them before the end of the cross-examination, and even if I do, I would need in any event -- I would need to study these documents, and perhaps I would also need to talk with investigators. And since your decision is that this witness cannot be brought here for direct examination before the 15th of January - and that will be today, or rather, we started him yesterday - because this witness made his first statement - and of course in my cross-examination, I will raise it - because he made his first statement a month and a half ago, I should like to ask this Honourable Court to give the Defence tomorrow afternoon, once we get these documents, to be able to study them, to talk with investigators, and conduct our cross-examination tomorrow afternoon. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have to hear the response from the Prosecutor. Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have prepared a pile of documents my learned colleague is talking about. Unfortunately, these documents are attachments to our witness's prior statement. For some reason, they were not disclosed to the Defence. Actually, we used only one document from this pile of documents as our exhibit, and it has been disclosed to the Defence. Precisely, it was disclosed yesterday. Just -- I mean, the certificate of membership we have already discussed here in the courtroom. As for the rest of the documents, they are ready for disclosure and the Defence can have them in their domain. There are not -- there are not any long documents which require a lot of time for the preparation, just some minor documents. At least, they seem to be minor for the Prosecution while we were deciding whether to use them as exhibits or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, but it will be fair for the Defence to have all those documents long beforehand, so that they could prepare their cross-examination in due time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, I understand the situation, Your Honour. But you know, this is one of our more recent witnesses, and there is some time needed for the translation and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any witnesses waiting after this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am sorry -- my apology to Mr. Poriouvaev. I think this is -- raises a more general matter. No, we had fully anticipated this witness would take the day. And I think if cross-examination proceeded at this time, it would in fact take the day. So we have not planned on having -- calling another witness until tomorrow. As Mr. Poriouvaev has indicated, this witness statement was provided to the Defence counsel a long time ago. It clearly states on its face, makes reference to attachments. Now we admit it was our oversight. Usually when witnesses statements are turned over, any attachments go simultaneously. For whatever reason, by oversight they were not. However, I think it's fair to point out that counsel have had the statement for a long time, it makes clear and abundant reference to the fact there are attachments. There was never any issue raised until just a few moments ago that they had not received those. They could have asked at any time in the past six weeks to be provided with those documents, which as counsel, my colleague, indicates are not voluminous. We are talking about a very small number, several pages of documents. Now, again it is our oversight, for which we have apologised and, which we have remedied within minutes of it being brought to our attention. It could have been bought to our attention in December. It wasn't. And that's where we are, Your Honour. But no, because of the planning purposes, we do not have a witness other than this witness to finish the day and we fully anticipated that this witness would complete the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, I believe it is your obligation to disclose all the documents, as well as attachments, to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Only by doing so is it fair to the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've explained our position. I agree with you. I've explained what happened. I can't give you another answer than that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the sake of the truth, we received the statements in the middle of this trial, sometime in November last year. So it is lesser than a month and a half ago. And we did not even know that this witness would be on the witness list. However, he turned up, and you decided that this witness could be called only recently, that is, only as late as December. And that is the truth, and both my learned friend and you know that, Your Honours. And until we knew that for certain, we could not get prepared, because all this time it was a very short. And once we started getting ready, we found that out. That was only a few days ago. When we realised that the witness would be testifying on Monday, we asked where are the documents. I mean, this was only an explanation for you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, after consultations with other Judges, we decided that the Defence counsel has the right to review all those documents and attachments to the statement of this witness. So the request from Defence counsel is granted. You will conduct your cross-examination of this witness tomorrow afternoon. If we finish with this witness today, if there is no other witnesses waiting for today, we just break until tomorrow. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I certainly am not standing to argue with the Chamber, but I do think it's fair, in light of the questions that have been raised. I'd like to tender to the Chamber the attachments just so you know exactly what it is. Because these are very, very limited documents. These are one-page documents with only a few sentences on each page or copies of an identification card. I'm not arguing counsel is not entitled to them but I think the Chamber should appreciate the fact when counsel says they need a day to prepare for these, I think the Chamber should see the nature of the documents. I'd give them -- tender them to the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, it's a matter of principle rather than how long the document is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour. But I still think it's only fair for the Chamber to see the documents that are being discussed. I think when counsel stands up and says they've been prejudiced by not having these documents, I think the Chamber should see what the documents are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I did not say the Defence counsel has been prejudiced at this moment, we just want to give enough time for the Defence counsel to prepare their case. You may submit all those documents to the Chamber, but we have already made a decision. We'll abide by that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: As I said Your Honour, I did not stand to re-argue your ruling. It's absolutely ruled, we're absolutely going to abide by it, of course. But I just simply think, for clarification sake, that the Chamber should have these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the usher could assist me, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I address some remarks on behalf of the Bench to, once again, counsel in this case. It has been brought to our attention that, on occasion, witnesses, and in particular the witness who is giving his evidence at the moment, have been upset or disturbed by loud comments that are emanating from counsel's bench. If we hear of any other occasion where Defence counsel make remarks that are derogatory or otherwise while the witness is giving testimony, we will consider holding those counsel in contempt. Is that understood? We spoke about this only last week. Comments in relation to witnesses are to stop. We take this very, very seriously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness, please. Yes, Mr. Prosecutor, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Witness, I asked you just to read the document. Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I haven't finished it. There was just a small part that I still need to read. Yes, I have finished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I ask you about this document for two reasons. The first reason: Did you see the name of your unit in this document?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, because in the English translation, again, we have a mistake, a misprint; "Branko Penavic." And my question will be: Was Stela's unit also considered as an elite unit, like yours?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever cooperate together in carrying out some military action -- military or other actions, apart from those already mentioned by you when you were fighting together just at the bottom of the hum?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember any situation that there was some conflict between your commander and Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you briefly inform the Trial Chamber what happened and who solved that problem.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what happened, I'd rather not talk about it. According to what I heard from Baja, there was to be a meeting with -- at Tuta's, and the -- and the situation which had arisen between those two units was to be resolved in a correct manner, in a nice manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, was the situation solved?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was solved, because there were no incidents after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit number P702. Witness, I just would like you to read the first page of the document, just two first paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've done that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, according to this document, that those two units, Vinko Skrobo and Benko Penavic, were set up in April 1993, according to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you know any members -- or do you remember any members of your unit now?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some of them I do remember. I remember some names, and others I might only recognise if I saw their photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, could you give us some names to the extent you remember them.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can mention Benito, Sadzak, Seno Mahmutovic, Fadil Duric, Zubac, Cape or Capa, Jakov.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jakov, do you remember his nickname? I mean Jakov.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the person whose name is Robert Medic?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember a person whose name is Miroslav Kolubara?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember. All right. If you don't remember, you don't remember. And now I would like you to -- the witness should be shown Exhibit number 588. I would like you to take a look at the second page of the B/C/S version, just the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one question based on this document: According to this document, there were some problems with a unit called Mrmak and Benko Penavic, who, due to the frequent transfer of civilians toward that part of the Bulevar, made arrangements for exchanges of prisoners on private business. Do you know if such kind of private exchanges of prisoners take place in your area of responsibility, I mean your unit?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you briefly inform the Trial Chamber how did this system work, of private exchanges.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not really familiar with the system. I know that behind the system was Baja. He was sending prisoners to the other side, and certain things he also sent to the other side, and in exchange requested something from the east side. I cannot remember anything specific, but I remember very well how prisoners crossed from the west to the east side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. My last question will be -- it's about Exhibit number 620.1. I would like the witness to be shown this exhibit. Witness, what I will ask you: In the previous part of your testimony, you explained to the Trial Chamber the manner in which cleansing operations were being carried out in your area of responsibility. Now I would like you to read the document and maybe you can compare. Were your operations organised in the same way, I mean within your unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am lodging an objection to this question. It is perhaps a little late. But when you look at the document a little bit closer, I believe this question is tantamount to an attempt to -- it's a document which is incriminating against my client is -- if I understand the question, the Prosecutor is trying to -- somehow trying to show how these operations were allegedly taking place. This document in itself, which does not only contain the description -- I think that he -- the question is being asked to elaborate on how it was done, even though we have a description. Why are we now being offered another document, which has nothing to do with his unit, in order to go back to this question? And this is just an attempt to have this reintroduced, and I therefore object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, I'm not quite sure about what your question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: My question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please rephrase your question and put it in a more clear way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, I will try to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just while talking about the cleansing operation, you, Witness AC, explained to the Trial Chamber the manner in which your operations were carried out -- prepared and then carried out. If you read this document, is it the same manner that in your area of responsibility the operations were prepared and carried out in the same way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the same objection. We believe that this question is not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, you have to ask specific questions to this witness to describe in what way his unit was doing at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Witness AC, this document refers to October -- September/October. Did your unit carry out the operation -- cleansing operations at that time?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not be able to say whether it was in July, August, January, February, March, April, but these operations were conducted throughout the period when I was with the ATG Benko Penavic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you leave ATG Benko Penavic?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they allow - I mean your commanders - to leave the unit?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Poriouvaev.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'm loath to ask you how to do something or say to you how you should do it, but perhaps it might be of assistance to the Trial Chamber if you were to ask this witness to describe a typical cleansing operation that he personally engaged in, and then maybe we could draw our own conclusions from the document, whether it differed or otherwise from what is alleged in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Witness, now the Trial Chamber would like us to ask you of a description of some typical cleansing operation in which you were personally involved. Just you maybe take some seconds and try to recall the most prominent one or notorious one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Defence of Mr. Mladen Naletilic would object to the question based on the fact that we feel it's very improper to give the witness a document which describes a certain activity and then ask later on, after he's allowed to read that document, to describe how he may have conducted such operations or some unit that he allegedly was involved in may have conducted it, after he's already been allowed to read a document which purports to show how some other unit allegedly carried out the operations. So we object on those grounds, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, we also read that document, and we believe that document is very general, is not a detailed one. And Judge Clark has already mentioned to Mr. Prosecutor about some specific details of that cleansing operation conducted by the unit the witness was belonging to. You may proceed, Witness, to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would happen like this: The persons who were supposed to be conducting these types of operations of cleansing of ethnic population knew each other. I was one of these persons. What we did was we would come to certain neighbourhoods which were predesignated by Baja to be ethnically cleansed. We would come with both trucks and private cars. When we would come to the neighbourhood which was to be cleansed, personnel would be assigned to all cardinal points so that we would protect this so-called cleansing operation. I was one of those who was guarding and protecting this quadrant or the neighbourhood. The others would enter the apartments on which on the front doors they would find Muslim names. If they weren't sure whether the person in question was of Muslim background, they were to knock on the door and ask for the necessary documents. Keys would then be taken away from these people and handed over to Baja. The persons who were detained or expelled from the apartments would then be loaded onto the trucks. At first, the men would be taken to the Heliodrom and women and children over to the other bank. And in cases -- and if there were altogether, like the case was in the Pentagon -- the Pentagon was another neighbourhood -- it was the name of a neighbourhood -- then that could have been done as well. People were then pushed. Sometimes they would be hit with the pistol or rifle butts, their jewellery would be stripped from them, and they would be mistreated in various ways too. After the operation was concluded, the detainees would be taken to these predesignated locations and Baja issued a strict order to the effect that, on that day and until Baja says otherwise, people were not to revisit the locations where the ethnic cleansing had been carried out. Then after that, Baja would go in with his people and empty the neighbourhood -- that is, the apartments which had been vacated. After that, he would give permission to other members of ATG to freely go into the neighbourhood and find the apartment of their liking and appropriate it. I think this, in brief, would sort of sum up how these actions were carried out. I want to point out that -- that we did not work along with the military police, but rather, we carried these -- carried out these operations on our own. Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 7958 to 7963.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And my final question: Did you ever see HV units while you were a member of the Benko Penavic unit?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I would have gone back to Prozor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You should not -- I've got your response and am satisfied with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: That's the end of my examination-in-chief, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Par, are you going to do your cross-examination today or you defer it to tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not prepared to do it today, and I -- I don't know about tomorrow, but I would like to leave the decision for tomorrow. What I'm trying to say: If I had any questions tomorrow, it would be one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I'm afraid we have to keep you here for another day. As I warned you before, during your stay here, you are still under the oath, so do not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody approach you about your testimony here. When the usher pulls down the blinds, you may leave the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you. I have a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To whom is your question going to address? To the Chamber? To the Prosecutor? Or to the Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whoever is competent for that. It has to do with -- it has to do with one of the forms here. And I would like to go back to it and comment on it, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, you may ask some questions in this aspect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which form do you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which form do you mean? Do you mean some certain document?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document P556.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to go back to that document tomorrow or perhaps even at the very end of the examination, I would like to ask a question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you want to inform the Trial Chamber on some issue stemming from this document?

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would prefer if I could have this document kept aside, and then if I can go back to it and ask a question about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you are not authorised to ask questions in the courtroom. You are supposed to answer questions. If you don't understand something in the question which is directed to you by the Prosecutor, by the Judge, or by the counsel, then you may ask a question. If you want to give some explanations relevant to this document, you may do that, because sometime ago I asked some questions relevant to this document.

utterances.speaker: Witness AC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I apologise, and let us simply forget my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may leave now, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, because we have a little bit of time, I would like to make a submission very briefly. Not -- thank you. Not only is it absolutely acceptable what Judge Clark said, but this is what -- how things should be in any courtroom anywhere in the world. I would like to say something that is well known to all of us, and I would, after that, like to get some directions from you. The hearings are a live process. We don't know what to expect. It's unpredictable. The Defence cannot know what is going to happen. If we were to know what was going to happen, this trial would not be necessary, just as any other trial would not be necessary. This is why we need to consult among the Defence counsel at various stages of the trial, and especially during the cross-examination. I will say that we never commented to witnesses nor did we ever directly address them. Perhaps we could have been louder or more eloquent among ourselves, and because we speak the same language as the witnesses do, it is possible - I say it is possible - that some witnesses may have heard something, some of our exchanges, which may or may not have benefitted the cross-examination. And I was a judge for a number of -- for many years, and I know that it is unpleasant to give testimony. And I myself have been in a situation to do that, and I felt very uncomfortable. So I say it is possible that some of the witnesses may have overheard some of our exchanges which were simply and exclusively meant to do the -- to provide the best defence that we can. If this has happened, I do apologise sincerely to Judge Clark. This was not done intentionally. So perhaps, Mr. President, Your Honours, we can get some directions from you how to conduct this communication. If we were to write notes to each other back and forth, that will take a lot of time. We, the Croats, are one of the Mediterranean people, and I think that our temperament is probably a little bit different. And again, I apologise one more time. Of course what Judge Clark said is not only to be respected but it is something that would be normal in any courtroom. So -- but perhaps, yes, we could be a little bit quieter too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, we take note of what you said just now, and we also believe that in all the jurisdictions, the communication between the counsel and his client should be confidential. The written communication between the counsel and his client is greatly encouraged in this courtroom, and sometimes you may approach to your client to consult with him on certain points. But you should not make the conversation louder or more eloquent among yourselves. It is not proper for us, as well as for the witness, to hear your conversation, which might be mistakenly regarded as some threat from the Defence bench. I'm not blaming you on that issue, I just remind you on this very point. Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I think that we have fully understood the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, according to your witness schedule, are we going to -- are we going to hear the next witness tomorrow morning, or we'll continue with the cross-examination with this witness? We read all the documents you kindly furnished to the Chamber. We realised they are not extensive one, they are very simple one. We believe the Defence counsel have the whole afternoon to go through all those documents and to prepare their cross-examination. And also taking into consideration of the time schedule of this trial, tomorrow morning we are still in the morning session, which means we'll start at 9.00 and finish by 1.45. There's no afternoon session at all. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you very much for raising that. I think that it makes more sense, although ultimately, I suppose obviously, we're in the Chamber's hands, but given what comments that, Mr. President, you just made, it seems to make the most sense to complete this witness tomorrow without yet again interrupting another witness, which sometimes we've had to do, but there seems not a reason to do so in this occasion. We can complete this witness and then proceed to the next witness, following the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So tomorrow morning, we'll start with the cross-examination of the present witness. And at the same time, we would like to entrust the registrar to inform all the sections of this Tribunal to abide by the trial's scheduling, because we don't have much time to lose, since the case of the Prosecution is approaching to its end. We will adjourn until 9.00 in courtroom 1 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
